h: Brize Norton, Witney and the West Oxfordshire Edge
p: Crocodiles of the World sits at Brize Norton, right next to the biggest RAF station in the country, so don't be surprised if a huge grey transport plane rumbles overhead while you're watching the crocs. Plane-spotting kids get a bonus show.

Carterton itself grew up around RAF Brize Norton and is a practical, friendly town with supermarkets and cafés for supplies. For something prettier, Witney is a short drive east, a market town on the River Windrush once famous for blanket-making. Its old Buttercross and church green make a nice wander, and Cogges Manor Farm, a historic farm with animals, a manor house and gardens, sits on the edge of town and is a lovely pairing for younger children.

Burford, with its steep high street of honey-coloured stone, is only a few miles north-west, and the Cotswold Wildlife Park is just beyond it, so animal-loving families can easily build a two-day trip around the area.

Tips: the zoo is compact, so a couple of hours usually does it. Keeper talks are where you'll learn the most, including how to tell an alligator from a crocodile. Indoor houses can be warm and humid, so layers you can strip off are handy in winter.
